item.title: Feature: 15 Years Ago, 'Return To Dream Land' Ushered In Kirby's Golden Era

description.p: Kirban legend.Kirby has always been one of Nintendo's more consistently successful franchises. While the little pink puffball never had anything remotely resembling a 'dark era' like many other Nintendo series, there was a time around the turn of the century where Kirby began to spin his wheelies a bit.After the 2000 release of Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards, developer HAL Laboratory immediately began work on Kirby’s next big adventure. Glimmers of a mainline Kirby title for the GameCube featuring the return of the helper system from Kirby Super Star with four-player co-op popped up in various circles over the years, including E3 2005, but a full-on game never materialised.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Gallery: iam8bit's Sonic Legacy Cartridges Are Stunning, But Are They Worth The Money?

description.p: For a select few, potentially.When iam8bit announced its Legacy Cartridge Collection for Sonic and Sonic 2 on Sega Genesis a few months back, it's safe to say that most people were taken aback by the price. Available via iam8bit's official store page, each cartridge — complete with authentic case, instruction manual, and poster — is priced at $99.99.That's a lot. Certainly a hefty chunk more than both games cost together digitally on Switch. Hell, you can pick up Sonic Origins Plus for 20 quid these days. So no, for the Average Joe who just wants to play these games in whichever manner is most convenient, these are probably not worth the money.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
